prompt:
Create a polished design-review board with TWO fully rendered responsive landing-page compositions: desktop left, portrait mobile right. Use the supplied website as edit target and reference for “Water and light”, Žemaitija Country Escapes. Preserve its cool mineral-grey ground, dark forest ink, restrained lake-blue accent, humanist sans, wooded-shore horizon photograph, horizontal search band and flat three-accommodation text index. High resolution landscape board showing actual desktop 1440×1100 equivalent and recomposed 390×1350 portrait mobile, no device frames, browser chrome or perspective.
Correct both views: remove tree-and-wave logo and invented brand tagline; use full brand wordmark. Keep heading “Let the day slow down.” on opaque light ground ABOVE photograph, not on clouds. Arrival and Departure empty “Select date”; never 2025. Top-visible readable disclosure “Fictional portfolio demo · AI-generated illustrations · No real bookings”. Regional lake photo has NO buildings, docks or amenities; caption on an opaque strip reads “Illustrative regional landscape · No property lake access is implied”. The lower meadow property photo is separate and labelled “Illustrative property concept”. Accommodation index lists Forest Cottage up to 2 guests, Lakeside Cabin up to 2 guests, Family Cottage up to 6 guests; no invented facility or proximity copy. No eyebrow headings. Navigation Stays / Compare / Manage booking / Lietuvių / English / Deutsch. On mobile use an intentionally short horizon crop, stacked labelled booking controls, conspicuous “Check availability”, then all three readable accommodation entries. Keep cool landscape rhythm distinct from warm paper and timber-led concepts. Outside-page label “C — Water and light”.

lineage.prompt: Create a high-fidelity English desktop website composition for “Žemaitija Country Escapes”, a fictional Lithuanian countryside accommodation booking demo inspired by the Plateliai area. Render the actual web page edge to edge, crisp legible UI, landscape 1440×1100 equivalent, no browser frame or surrounding objects. Real content: Forest Cottage, up to 2 guests; Lakeside Cabin, up to 2 guests; Family Cottage, up to 6 guests. Header includes the full brand, “Stays”, “Compare”, “Manage booking”, and “Lietuvių / English / Deutsch”. Show a real-looking availability form with persistent labels Accommodation, Arrival, Departure, Guests and primary action “Check availability”. No availability results or invented price. Prominent readable disclosure: “Fictional portfolio demo · AI-generated illustrations · No real bookings”. Label every property illustration “Illustrative property concept”. Do not invent amenities, reviews, locations, lake access or heritage status. Photorealistic illustrative scenes should reflect documented Samogitian timber rural buildings: broad hipped or half-hipped roofs, modest low timber walls, restrained detail, meadow and mixed spruce/birch woodland, temperate soft light. These are creative interpretations, not reconstructions or real-property photography. Avoid Mediterranean villas, Alpine chalets, Nordic glass cabins, amenities and generic accommodation cards. Direction C, “Water and light”: pale cool mineral grey and muted lake-blue, dark forest ink links; elegant wide-set humanist sans headings. The page rhythm is a photographic essay in horizontal horizons: quiet heading “Let the day slow down.” above an expansive open-water and wooded-shore panorama, with NO building, dock, boats or facilities at the water. Caption clearly reads “Illustrative regional landscape · No property lake access is implied”. Directly below, an opaque deep forest band carries the availability form with warm paper controls. Below it, three accommodation names and capacities make a flat comparison-like text index, alongside a second narrower meadow-and-timber photograph labelled illustrative. Navigation is spacious and typographic. Clear booking purpose, visible demo disclosure, no floating panels, gradients, badges, rounded cards or blue resort clichés. The dominant move is the horizon and its horizontal reading rhythm, not a centred headline with three cards.
